newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares saddled with losses in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares saddled with losses in bourse trade.

text.p: German shares were saddled with losses in bourse trade on Thursday, ending the session down in listless trading as the market searched for fuel to launch a new advance on record levels.

The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session down 11.58 points at 3,562.11 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day dealings, was down 28.95 points at 3,559.62 as the selling pressure showed no initial signs of abating.

Traders said options expiries on the DAX index and on shares would likely keep the market on the downside. Another factor was next Tuesday's FOMC meeting and the ongoing debate whether the Federal Reserve will raise U.S. interest rates.
"There's not much room for movement right now and it looks as though we are going to be locked in somewhat volatile range trade," said one Frankfurt dealer.
Carmakers, hurt by the weaker dollar, were steady to lower despite the VDA German automobile association reporting a 15 percent year-on-year rise in vehicle production.
Volkswagen AG ended down four marks at 1,149 marks and Daimler-Benz AG was down 10 pfennigs at 134.20 marks.

BMW AG ended down 35 marks at 1,430 marks despite the Munich-based carmaker reporting on Thursday a provisional 17.4 percent rise in five-month sales to 24.3 billion marks and a nearly eight percent rise in vehicle deliveries to 497,000 for the period from January to May.
Chemical shares were mixed despite the weaker dollar.

BASF AG fell despite saying its 1997 sales would top 50 billion marks and that sales and profits would remain at high levels in the coming months. BASF shares pared some of their losses to end down 17 pfennigs at 67.28 marks.
But rival Hoechst AG ended up 15 pfennigs at 65.85 marks and Bayer AG rose 25 pfennigs to 65.20 marks amid shifting within the sector.
